expansion:
A is correct. This is an arcuate scotoma: a dense curved field defect arising from the blind spot and arching around fixation toward the nasal field, following the arcuate retinal nerve-fibre bundles (not taken from the course material). In open-angle glaucoma, the lecture links neural rim thinning to visual-field changes and specifically lists “Arcuate scotomata (superior, inferior)” (L11, page 14). The described chronic glaucoma setting and arcuate configuration therefore fit this named defect.

B is wrong because a central scotoma is centred on fixation rather than curving from the blind spot around it. The course illustrates central scotoma as a central oval defect in acute optic neuritis (L21, slide 4).

C is wrong because bitemporal hemianopia is loss of the temporal outer half of each eye’s field, not a local curved scotoma. The lecture’s chiasmal field figure shows the outer temporal halves lost with nasal halves spared (L22, slide 15).

D is wrong because homonymous hemianopia is loss of the same half of the visual field in both eyes, typically from a post-chiasmal lesion, rather than an arcuate defect associated with glaucoma. The lecture describes a left homonymous hemianopia as loss of the left half in both eyes (L22, slide 17).
objective: Recognize arcuate scotoma as a characteristic glaucomatous visual-field defect.
